Looking at this properly, Option A is the logic of the emergency room, not the conservation studio. In my field, "acting now" on incomplete information is how we get those disastrous over-cleanings and aggressive inpaintings that strip a painting of its history. You do not touch the surface until you know exactly what you are touching.

Option B is the only defensible position. Documentation is not passive; it is the primary act of preservation. If you intervene before you have fully understood the material history—the layers, the previous repairs, the specific chemistry of the degradation—you are not saving the object; you are altering it based on a guess.
